title: A split commutative coideal inclusion is faithfully flat
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. A commutative Hopf $k$-algebra here means a unital commutative $k$-algebra $A$ with $k$-algebra maps $\Delta_A:A\to A\otimes_k A$, $\epsilon_A:A\to k$, $S_A:A\to A$ such that $(\Delta_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=(1\otimes\Delta_A)\Delta_A$, $(\epsilon_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=(1\otimes\epsilon_A)\Delta_A=1_A$, and $\mu_A(S_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=\mu_A(1\otimes S_A)\Delta_A=\eta_A\epsilon_A$, under the usual tensor unit and associativity identifications; $\mu_A$ and $\eta_A$ are multiplication and unit. Tensor products are those of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Let $B$ be such a commutative Hopf $k$-algebra, let $A$ be a unital commutative $k$-algebra, and let $i:A\to B$ be an injective $k$-algebra homomorphism. Suppose that for every $a\in A$, $\Delta_B(i(a))$ belongs to the image of $i\otimes1_B:A\otimes_k B\to B\otimes_k B$ (the right coideal condition). Regard $B$ as an $A$-module through $i$. Assume there exists an $A$-linear map $r:B\to A$ with $r\circ i=1_A$. Then $B$ is a faithfully flat $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. Neither $A$ nor $B$ is required to be finite-dimensional or finitely generated; no Hopf structure on $A$ is assumed.

source.place: Bichon, arXiv:2301.05480v2, Theorem 1.1 and the bimodule conditional-expectation convention preceding section 2, specialized to commutative algebras. Read online at https://arxiv.org/html/2301.05480v2; local document WANTED in report.md. Commutativity turns the stated A-linear retraction into the required A-bimodule retraction.

proof.text: Identify $A$ with its image in $B$ using the injective algebra map $i$, and write $H=B$, $E=r$. This identification carries the given tensor-image condition to $\Delta_H(A)\subseteq A\otimes_kH$: tensoring an injective map of vector spaces with $H$ is injective (extend a basis). Commutativity and $A$-linearity give $E(ah a\prime)=aa\prime E(h)=aE(h)a\prime$ for $a,a\prime\in A$, $h\in H$. Also $E(1)=1$. Thus $E$ is a bimodule retraction. All constructions below use module tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Theorem 1.1 and conditional-expectation convention; elementary identification of the injected algebra with its image.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-hopf-module-kernels] to obtain $C=H/HA^+$, $L(M)=H\otimes_AM$ and its coaction, for every $A$-module $M$. Write $R(X)$ for its coinvariants. For $X=L(M)$ the isomorphism [lem-sfb-coideal-canonical-tensor-isomorphism] gives $\kappa_X:H\otimes_A(H\otimes_AM)\simeq C\otimes_k(H\otimes_AM)$. If $z=\sum h_t\otimes m_t$ is coinvariant, its coaction formula says $\kappa_X(\sum h_t\otimes1\otimes m_t)=\pi(1)\otimes z=\kappa_X(1\otimes z)$. Injectivity of $\kappa_X$ gives $\sum h_t\otimes1\otimes m_t=\sum1\otimes h_t\otimes m_t$. Apply the balanced map $h\otimes h\prime\otimes m\mapsto E(h)h\prime\otimes m$. The two sides become $1\otimes\sum E(h_t)m_t$ and $z$, respectively. Hence every coinvariant is $1\otimes m$. The map $e_M:H\otimes_AM\to M$, $h\otimes m\mapsto E(h)m$, is well-defined by $A$-linearity and satisfies $e_M(1\otimes m)=m$. Thus $\eta_M:M\to R(L(M))$, $m\mapsto1\otimes m$, is bijective, with inverse $e_M|_{R(L(M))}$.

source.place: Propositions 2.3 (split case) and 2.4, with the two tensor maps written explicitly.

proof.text: For every relative Hopf module $X$, [lem-sfb-coideal-coinvariant-projection] supplies an $A$-linear retraction of $j_X:R(X)\hookrightarrow X$ and makes $1_H\otimes_Aj_X$ injective. Its hypotheses hold by step 1, with no finite-dimensionality assumption. By [lem-sfb-relative-hopf-counit-criterion] (1) this injectivity makes $\mu_X:H\otimes_AR(X)\to X$ injective, and by its part (2), applied with the retraction $E$ of step 1, $\mu_X$ is surjective. In particular, every $x\in X$ is a finite sum $\sum h_t x_t$ with $x_t\in R(X)$.

source.place: Lemma 2.6 and Proposition 2.7 (a) iff (b), with surjectivity of the counit under the conditional expectation.

proof.text: Let $f:M\hookrightarrow N$ be any injective $A$-linear map. By [lem-sfb-relative-hopf-module-kernels], $K=\ker L(f)$ is a relative Hopf module and $R(K)=K\cap R(L(M))$. A coinvariant of $K$, viewed in $L(M)$, is $1\otimes m$ by step 2. Its image in $L(N)$ is $1\otimes f(m)=0$; applying $e_N$ gives $f(m)=0$, so $m=0$. Hence $R(K)=0$. Step 3 applied to $X=K$ says $K$ is generated as an $H$-module by $R(K)$, and therefore $K=0$. Thus $1_H\otimes f$ is injective for every such $f$. Swapping tensor factors gives the convention in [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], so $H$ is flat over $A$.

source.place: Theorem 2.1 (1) implies (2), expanded as the underlying-kernel argument using the unit and counit.

proof.text: Consider a complex $M_1\xrightarrow{f}M_2\xrightarrow{g}M_3$. If it is exact, put $Z=\ker g=\operatorname{im}f$. The sequence $M_1\to M_2\to M_2/Z\to0$ remains exact after tensoring with $H$ by [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact]. The injection $M_2/Z\hookrightarrow M_3$ remains injective by step 4; its composite with the quotient map is $g$. This proves exactness of the tensored complex. Conversely, suppose the tensored complex is exact and $y\in\ker g$. Then $1\otimes y$ is in its middle kernel, so $1\otimes y=\sum h_t\otimes f(x_t)$. Applying $e_{M_2}$ from step 2 gives $y=\sum E(h_t)f(x_t)=f(\sum E(h_t)x_t)$. Thus $\ker g\subseteq\operatorname{im}f$; the reverse inclusion follows from $gf=0$. Tensoring therefore preserves and reflects exactness of every complex, exactly [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. This proves the assertion for $B=H$ with its specified $A$-module structure.

The item statement is the commutative case of Thm 1.1: an A-linear retraction is a bimodule map because H is commutative, and the coideal condition becomes Δ(A)⊆A⊗H since i⊗1 is injective over a field. Faithful flatness matches def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map. Steps 1, 2, 4 and 5 check by hand: the balanced map h⊗h'⊗m↦E(h)h'⊗m, e_M well-defined, the kernel argument, and preservation plus reflection through right exactness and e_{M2}. The kernels, canonical-tensor and projection nodes are true and not duplicates; checks include J=HA⁺ being a coideal, κ well-defined exactly because Δ(A)⊆A⊗H, and the inverse killing HA⁺. Fault (E2/E5): lem-sfb-relative-hopf-counit-criterion stated 1⊗j_X injective ⇒ μ_X bijective with no retraction. Bichon's proof of (a)⇒(c) only asserts that the tensored row is exact. Under κ that exactness is equivalent to μ_X being surjective, so the step is circular. With E, q=(E⊗1)κ⁻¹ is A-linear and satisfies qδ=p−1, which splits the row. FIX: the node now states (1) μ_X injective ⇔ 1⊗j_X injective, and (2) μ_X surjective given an A-linear E with E|_A=1. Item step 3 is re-worded to cite (1) and (2); its uses are unchanged. Clarity fix (B2) on canonical-tensor: H⊗_A X = L(X) for X restricted to A. Accepted tool_use: lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact, a generic leaf.
